title: Session-affinity precedence and safe rollout coordination for version pins across region/tier fallbacks
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: As we roll out model versions (canary/A-B) and allow session or user-level model pins, overlapping policy sources (admin pins, session pins, cohort assignment, geo/tier routing) create ambiguity about which model variant should serve a request when capacity or region constraints require fallback. This ticket defines deterministic precedence rules, session-affinity TTL semantics, and a safe degrade strategy that preserves rollout guarantees (cohort ratios) while enforcing region/tier constraints and minimizing customer-visible regressions.

Goal: Produce an implementable spec and integration tests for the routing resolver that enforce: (1) clear precedence among pin sources; (2) TTL-based session pin decay and re-assignment algorithm; (3) cohort preservation under geo/tier fallback (weight-preserving degrade); (4) automatic rollback thresholds and kill-switch integration; (5) observability hooks for per-cohort error/latency drift.

Acceptance criteria:
- Spec doc versioned at Confluence (link in comments).
- Resolver behavior implemented behind a feature flag.
- Integration tests that simulate region loss and verify cohort distribution approximates target weights after fallback.
- End-to-end canary with automatic rollback when cohort error-rate > 3x baseline for 10 minutes.
- Telemetry chart in Datadog showing request split by pin-source + cohort + fallback-reason.

Constraints and trade-offs: 
- Strict preservation of cohort ratios is expensive when cross-tier routing requires model variant substitution (e.g., quantized variant in lower tier). We'll prefer approximate weight-preservation where exact ratios are impossible.
- Deterministic behavior must be compatible with existing session sticky rules (session-id hashing) to avoid oscillation.
- Short TTLs increase exposure to routing churn; long TTLs delay rollout reach. We need a compromise TTL default and an adaptive decay for low-traffic sessions.

Out of scope: low-level kernel selection and quantization strategy (handled by runtime), developer-facing rollout UI updates (handled by Console team separately).
comments: 2026-02-22 - Sync: Drafted initial precedence list. Proposal: admin_pin > project_pin (per-route) > session_pin (sticky) > cohort_rollout_assignment > region_tier_policy > default_model. Raised question about whether session_pin should honor explicit version affinity when a route-level project pin exists. (Liam)

2026-02-25 - Decision: session pins remain honored only if they are for a variant that is compatible with the selected region/tier. If not compatible, resolver will attempt cohort-preserving fallback (see pseudocode). This avoids silently breaking session expectations while keeping services online. (Design review)

Salt rotates per rollout to support rolling cohort reshuffle; documented edge cases. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/7890 (diffs include resolver + tests). (Priya)

Scenario: Canary assigned 10% traffic in us-west-2 but canary model only exists in dedicated-tier in us-east-1 -> fallback should route 10% of total global requests to canary-compatible variant or a best-fit variant while flagging cohort_mismatch in telemetry. Tests currently pass in simulated env. (QA)

Implementation pseudocode (for resolver):

- inputs: request {session_id, route_id, region_preference, tier_preference, explicit_version_pin} 
- compute: pin_sources = [admin_pin(route), project_pin(route), explicit_version_pin, session_pin(session_id), cohort_assignment(route_id, session_id), region_tier_policy(route, region_preference, tier_preference)]
- iterate pin_sources in precedence order; for candidate_variant in pin_source: 
    if variant.available_in(region_preference, tier_preference): return candidate_variant, pin_source_reason
    else collect: fallback_candidates by compatible_variants_across_tiers(variant.family)
- if no exact available_variant: run weight_preserving_selector(fallback_candidates, cohort_weights) -> returns best_fit_variant and adjustment_reason
- if still nothing: return default_model_for_route with reason 'forced_fallback'

Note: weight_preserving_selector tries to map cohort membership to available variants by solving a simple knapsack-style allocation to minimize deviation from target cohort percentages. This is approximate and runs with a timeout of 5ms in hot path. (Engineering)

Open questions: 
- TTL defaults: propose session_pin.ttl = 24h for interactive apps, 7d for long-running sessions (configurable). Should we expose TTL override per-project? (product decision)
- Salt rotation frequency: monthly by default to enable reshuffle, but must be coordinated with rollout windows to avoid churn.
- Should we prefer lower-quality quantized variants in same region over higher-quality remote variants when latency SLOs are strict? (trade-off between quality and latency).

Next steps:
- Finalize spec in Confluence and attach to PR.
- Add e2e canary pipeline: create canary that exercises cross-region fallback and automated rollback rule.
- Measure telemetry and set alerts for cohort drift > 5% vs expected within 30 minutes.
- Product: decide TTL exposure and default values.
